summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that Tom Allen offered to fight any man in America for $500 to $10,000 under London prize ring rules, would meet Joe Coburn in Wyoming Territory, and rated Mike McCoole only No. 3 as a fighter.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Missouri Republican—St. Louis, December 1, 1869', matching the date. The item is under the SPORTING heading.

facts.fact: Allen offered to fight any man in America for $500 to $10,000 in a stand-up fight under London prize ring rules
Allen offered to meet Joe Coburn, whom he called the leading scientific pugilist in the United States, anywhere in Wyoming Territory
Allen said McCoole was very good as a private citizen but stood No. 3 as a fighter, and had a bad crowd of backers
Billy Carroll was authorized to make arrangements for Allen's fights; challengers had to deposit at least $100 with the New York Clipper or the Sporting Times of Boston

notes: Allen's opinions are paraphrased by the paper, not quoted, so no quote text is recorded.
